- `flag:--cv` -- BLOCKED, not green. Verified directly: ran the pinned CLI oracle (tools/oracle/cli/bin/catboost-v1.2.10, v1.2.10) `fit --cv Classical:{0,1,2};3 --cv-no-shuffle` against R's `catboost.cv(fold_count = 3, type = "Classical", shuffle = FALSE)`, same params (iterations=10, depth=2, learning_rate=0.3, random_seed=42, loss_function=Logloss, boosting_type=Plain, thread_count=1, use_best_model=FALSE) and the same shared numeric-only dataset (tests/fixtures/oracle-cli/smoke_data.csv). The two produce entirely different per-iteration test-metric curves for every fold (not a reordering) because they run different native code paths: the CLI's fit/eval-feature/model-based-eval/select-features `--cv` flag is parsed into TCvDataPartitionParams (catboost/private/libs/options/cross_validation_params.h) at data-load time to pick a single train/test split (fold n of k) -- used by catboost/libs/train_lib/eval_feature.cpp's single-split path -- while R's catboost.cv binds directly to CrossValidate() (catboost/libs/train_lib/cross_validation.cpp), which builds and averages ALL k folds via the separate TCrossValidationParams struct. The matrix's matched_r_symbol=catboost.cv is a name-based match, not a verified mechanism match; per spec 4.4 this is left red rather than fabricated green. catboost.cv itself is real, extensively tested surface (test_model.R, test_params_validation.R) -- the gap is specifically the CLI --cv flag's own data-partition code path, which the R package has no binding for.

- `param:graph` -- catboost-8z4.122 re-verification: confirmed the R-side glue itself is wired correctly (src/catboostr.cpp reuses the pairs code path for graph -- graphParam is validated identically to pairsParam and metaInfo.HasGraph is set from it, propagating correctly into TDataMetaInfo/TFeaturesLayout), so this is not an R-side marshaling bug as such -- it is a genuine native-side gap in the combination of graph= and group_id= on the in-memory matrix-Pool construction path specifically (data_provider_builders.cpp's SetGraph -> ConvertGraphToAdjMatrix / aggregated-feature-layout interaction with grouped queries), reproduced directly: building an R Pool with graph= and group_id= together throws a hard native/glue error (Internal CatBoost Error / Unimplemented from catboost.from_data_frame -> catboost.from_matrix -> data_provider_builders.cpp). graph is a real catboost.load_pool() arg (R/catboost.R:110) and a real Python Pool(graph=...) arg too, requiring nontrivial groups in both languages, and vendor/catboost/ is out of scope for this ticket. See test_params_validation.R.
- `param:input_borders` -- catboost-8z4.122 re-verification: input_borders remains absent from plain_options_helper.cpp (grepped directly, zero matches), confirming it is still never a recognized flat option -- unlike output_borders (a real flat option, OutputBordersFileName, see the green disposition for that row), input_borders is only ever consumed by Python's Pool.quantize() pre-processing step in the vendored core, never by the general PlainJsonToOptions flat-option parser catboost.train's params blob goes through in either language. Tied to the catboost.utils.quantize capability family (catboost-8z4.PT-C), not fixable within this ticket's scope. Verified directly: native rejects it with 'Unknown option {input_borders}' (plain_options_helper.cpp:512). See test_params_validation.R.
- `param:scale_pos_weight` -- catboost-8z4.122 re-verification, root cause now fully traced (not just reproduced): CreateMetrics() (catboost/libs/metrics/metric.cpp:6809-6822) unconditionally builds a metric object from the FULL objective/loss description -- including scale_pos_weight -- via CreateMetricFromDescription(objectiveMetricDescription, ...) to report the training-objective metric value, regardless of what eval_metric is set to (confirmed: this still fails even with eval_metric explicitly overridden to a bare 'Logloss', because the *objective* metric construction, not the eval metric construction, is what rejects it). CheckParameters (metric.cpp:6324) validates that objective-metric object against the same restricted per-metric-class ValidParamSets whitelist as any generic metric, and scale_pos_weight is a loss-gradient-only parameter never added to Logloss's metric ValidParamSets -- an upstream inconsistency between the loss builder (which does accept it) and the metric builder (which always runs too, and does not). No top-level flat scale_pos_weight option exists either (confirmed absent from plain_options_helper.cpp), and vendor/catboost/ is out of scope for this ticket, so there is no workaround available from R alone. See test_params_validation.R.

- `flag:--hosts-already-contain-loaded-data` -- catboost-inm: P10.A fix-round-1 left no justification for this row (empty tolerance_justification, no overlay entry) -- newly triaged for this ticket. Distributed-mode CLI-invocation-only mechanic, not a training option (code-verified): HostsAlreadyContainLoadedData is a field on TCatBoostOptions's load-params struct, set directly by CLI arg parsing (vendor/catboost/catboost/private/libs/app_helpers/bind_options.cpp:191-199) and never serialized into the plain JSON options that PlainJsonToOptions consumes. R's catboost.train() only ever sends that JSON (via prepare_train_export_parameters()) to the native trainer -- there is no path, even in principle, to set this field from R. It is also specific to the CLI's own multi-process master/worker launch (skip a redundant data reload on workers that already have the data), a concept the R package's single-process distributed-training support (file_with_hosts/node_type/node_port params, catboost-8z4.109) has no analog for.

R's own file-loading paths (read.csv/data.frame) handle CSV quoting themselves before the data ever reaches CatBoost's native bridge, so there is no R-level toggle for this CLI-parser-internal behavior to control.

Original finding: P10.A fix-round-1 (catboost-8z4.115 review findings): not applicable to R (verified via CLI --help: 'annotations to attach to all YT operations'): a Yandex distributed-cluster (YT) scheduling feature. This R package has no distributed/YT execution surface at all, so there is nothing for this flag to attach annotations to.
